title: Random-access retries and checksum repair playbook
content:
Summary:
This is a personal scratchpad for a recurring class of model-load failures where some worker processes hit EINVAL / short reads when doing random-access reads against sharded weight blobs in GCS. Behavior is intermittent across machines and seems correlated with larger instance types (higher concurrency) and when the same shard is requested by multiple processes concurrently.

Symptoms observed:
- Model serve logs show: ValueError: expected 5242880 bytes, got 4096 (offset mismatch)
- Python stacktrace highlights mmap or io.read returning fewer bytes than requested
- gsutil cp sometimes produces a file that passes sha256 locally, but process A and process B get different data when doing range GETs concurrently
- Failures occur more often after rolling kernel updates / container image update (suspicious)

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) On k8s node, spawn 4 processes that each do a ranged read of the same object at overlapping offsets.
2) Use a loop with curl range requests to mimic the serving runtime behavior.
3) Occasionally a process returns truncated data and loader emits mismatch.

Commands/diagnostics tried so far (history):
- Check full object integrity locally:
  gsutil cp gs://redwood-models/foo/model-0000.bin ./model-0000.bin
  sha256sum model-0000.bin  # expected value matches manifest

- Range GET sanity checks:
  curl -s -H "Range: bytes=1048576-2097151" \"https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-models/foo/model-0000.bin\" --output - | wc -c
  # expected 1048576 but sometimes returns 4096

- Using python requests to do concurrent ranged reads (local repro harness):
  import requests, threading
  def r(off, n):
      h={ 'Range': f'bytes={off}-{off+n-1}' }
      r = requests.get(url, headers=h, timeout=10)
      print(off, len(r.content))

- Observed a GCS error spike in cloud logging around the same time: 503 Internal Server Error for RewriteTo request (transient?)

- Verified server-side CRC32C and MD5 via gsutil hash -h
  gsutil hash -h model-0000.bin  # CRC32C matches manifest, MD5 not present for composed objects

- Tested gcsfuse mount to see if FUSE layer masks issue: attached blob to path, performed dd reads at offsets, behavior similar.

- Tried mmap fallback (changed loader to open(...).read instead of mmap) -- dropped incidence by ~60% but didn't eliminate.

Observed stacktraces / snippets captured:
- Loader exception: \"IOError: short read: requested 2097152 bytes at offset 4194304, got 4096\"
- Python stack (snippet):
  File \"/srv/loader/weights.py\", line 312, in _read_chunk
    buf = mm[offset:offset+length]
  IOError: could not allocate memory for slice (raised after short read)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) GCS range read across composed objects (many component uploads merged into single final object) yields cheap/reordered internal reads under high concurrency -> occasionally returns component boundary chunk instead of full range.
2) Kernel-level caching / page cache bug with gcsfuse / overlayfs causing stale page/frame mapping when multiple processes open same file concurrently (mmap-fallback improves but not perfect).
3) Intermediate proxy or edge (google frontends) returning transient 206 with wrong Content-Range header under high QPS.
4) Our serving runtime's prefetcher issues: overlapping concurrent read requests reuse same buffer/bytearray without copy and racing writes/clobbering occurs.

Evidence notes:
- Hypothesis #4 plausible: we saw one reproducible trace where two threads reused the same memoryview object returned from a pool; after enforcing copy() invariants, a set of failures disappeared in bench. But field incidents still persist.
- Hypothesis #1/3 plausible due to 503 spikes in cloud logs and occasional mismatched CRC logs on the backend.

Temporary mitigations that helped in prod (notes):
- Add per-object read mutex keyed by (object path, offset-block-index) to reduce concurrent overlapping range-GETs. Costs: increases latency under heavy load.
- Increase retry/backoff on short-read to perform up to 3 range retries with exponential backoff and revalidate CRC after full re-read.
- Prefer full-object download + mmap for hot shards (if object size < 1GiB) to avoid multiple range reads.

Commands to validate quick-fix locally: (examples)
- Reproducer harness (shell):
  for i in $(seq 1 50); do \
    curl -s -H \"Range: bytes=1048576-2097151\" \"$URL\" --output - | od -An -v -N 8 | md5sum &
  done | sort | uniq -c  # expect >1 unique MD5 if non-deterministic

- Retry pattern simulated in python:
  def ranged_get_with_retries(url, off, n):
      for attempt in range(3):
          r = requests.get(url, headers={ 'Range': f'bytes={off}-{off+n-1}' })
          if len(r.content) == n and validate_crc(r.content):
              return r.content
          time.sleep(0.2 * (2**attempt))
      raise IOError('short read after retries')

Longer-term next steps / TODOs:
- Instrumented run: add metrics to count short-read events per-object + include server-side returned headers (Content-Range, x-goog-hash) and worker-id in logs.
- Run a controlled large-scale test against a single composed object with concurrent N clients from different zones to try to trigger frontend inconsistencies.
- Ask GCP support for logs for the object (include time windows and trace ids) and escalate if we can reproduce within their time window.
- Replace gcsfuse usage for hot shards with ephemeral local cache + read-through mechanism.
- Audit buffer reuse in serving runtime (pooling paths) and add assertions in debug builds to ensure immutability of buffers when shared.

Quick notes for whoever picks this up next:
- Check commit 9f2b4d in serving-runtime: there was a perf patch that pooled memoryviews for range reads (revert/patch available in PR 2137).
- If you see CRC mismatch in logger but file-level sha256 matches manifest, suspect composed-object / component-level mismatch.
- Reproducer dir: /home/ira/repro/rand-read-2025-11 (local to my laptop)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are the short-reads correlated to storage class (nearline vs standard) or object composition (single upload vs composed)? Need a sweep.
- Does HTTPS front-end cache evict differently during kernel upgrades? Weird correlation observed with node restarts after security patch.
- Can we ship a small binary that does parallel ranged reads with HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 to check behavior difference?

Personal TODOs (for my next session):
- Finish adding per-object short-read metric and export to Prometheus (labels: object_path, offset_block, worker_type).
- Re-run large repro from three zones and capture headers with tcpdump (if allowed) or via proxy that logs headers.
- Draft note to GCP support with sample trace and times.

If you pick this up, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime and I can walk through the repro harness. Save a copy of any logs you collect (timestamped) and include the worker-id and kernel version.

-- Ira
